title: Glass Towers, Low Gear
brief: City pop instrumental, about three minutes: a night drive through a lit city. A groove that sits back, an electric bass that moves, electric piano chords rich in sevenths and ninths, bright synth brass stabs, and a tune one remembers after one hearing. The lead is a synthesizer (never a sampled saxophone or guitar). A verse, a chorus and a short solo.

sections.intent: Brass riff (the chorus departure line) previews the chorus cadence over EP, bass and a light groove
A-melo: low conversational lead with breaths; EP and bass carry the groove; no brass yet
B-melo: rising thirds in the hook rhythm tease the hook, held V bar thins, ii-V of IV pushes in
Sabi: hook stated, restated over new chords, departure up to B-flat 5, minor iv close
Brass riff returns with the guitar; turnaround to the verse
Verse restated with a higher departure and ending; brass answers; sixteenth hats
Pre-chorus with the string pad entering and a fuller build
Chorus with pad, shaker and more brass hits
Short synth solo over a minor-leaning cycle, quoting the hook, ride cymbal
Reduction: drums thin to rim and hats, D-flat maj9 surprise, ii-V into F
Chorus a whole step up in F: the arrival
Chorus again with a new top (D6, the peak) and a perfect close on the tonic
Brass riff in F, hook head on the last chord, final ritardando

tracks.name: Synth brass riff (intro, interlude, outro; doubles the last chorus)

decisions: Style: jpop/city-pop for every axis but tempo. Its tempo cell has no source, so tempo is borrowed from pop/disco (Harmonix funk/disco songs: median 119 BPM, middle 80% 109-131): city pop's rhythm trait names funk and disco, and 110 BPM sits at the low end of that range for a groove that sits back.

Melody and form have no source in the city pop entry: the brief gives verse, chorus and solo and about three minutes; climax-and-melody.md and arrangement.md give the srdc chorus, phrases with breaths, a peak saved for the last chorus, and the J-pop family's A-melo / B-melo / sabi turn.
Key E-flat major; the last two choruses and the outro a whole step up in F, prepared by a break that thins the band, turns to D-flat maj9 and takes ii-V into the new IV.
Chorus harmony starts from the royal road (IVM7-V7-iii7-vi) of the J-pop family, then goes its own way: ii9-V13-Imaj9-I9 and a minor iv (Abm6) before the tonic 6/9.

Hook: C-Eb-G rising to the major seventh of A-flat on a 3+3+2 sixteenth rhythm, then a repeated F and a D pushed over the bar line; restated over Fm9 (same notes, new colour), sequenced a third higher for the departure; the pre-chorus teases its head and turns it aside.
The intro, interlude and outro riff on synth brass is the chorus departure line, so the tune is heard before the chorus arrives.

Groove: blocks.drums soul feel in verses, funk feel in choruses and the solo (more ghost notes), ride in the solo, eighth hats in verse 1 and sixteenths from verse 2; snare backbeats 7 ms late and a 0.54 sixteenth swing in the rhythm section, the leads swung less and 6 ms behind.

Bass: written by template per section, root on the One, octaves, ghost notes (velocity 18 plays the bank's ghost samples), whole-step approaches from a chord tone into each change, diatonic sixteenth runs at phrase ends, and pushes with the brass into each chorus.
Electric piano: blocks.accompaniment syncopated comping (held in pre-choruses and the break), answering the melody and the bass, voiced rootless under the melody, notes lengthened to the next hit.
Layers held back: brass stabs from the pre-chorus and verse 2; guitar from chorus 1; pad and shaker from pre-chorus 2; the melody's D6 only in chorus 4.

authorship.composer: Claude (AI), working alone with the music-production skill 0.6.0

revision_history.change: First complete draft; its render stopped on the quiet-tail check.

Tail 8 s; voicing hygiene in dependency order; pad holds common tones; bass approaches chosen against the lead; solo states and restates an idea; interlude lighter, without guitar; final chord F6/9; high-passes lowered.

Lead +1.5 dB and solo +2 dB over a lighter backing; bass lower and fuller; pre-chorus V bar thinned; chorus 3 opens lighter, chorus 4 disco kick with open hats and the brass doubling the melody; riff on its own melody part.
Chorus phrases given breaths; lead 2 dB down through the pre-choruses; semitones inside EP, brass and guitar chords removed.
